The main takeaway from our work is that
, in many settings, interventions are a more powerful tool for causal discovery than passive observations.
, in many settings, the causal structure of a Bayesian network can be learned efficiently, even when the network is not acyclic.
, in the causal setting, a small number of interventions can be more informative than a large number of observations.
